title: Tissue Engineering by Intrinsic Vascularization in an In Vivo Tissue Engineering Chamber
protocol: Use rats weighing at least 250 g for their large size of vessels for creation of the arteriovenous loop.
Prepare the animal for surgery ensuring all instruments are properly sterilized and placed on sterile towels away from the surgical field to avoid contamination.
Anaesthetize the animal with 4% isoflurane inhalation.
Assess unresponsiveness to toe-pinch to confirm adequate anesthesia depth.
Maintain adequate anesthesia throughout the procedure using 2% isoflurane.
Place the animal in a supine position on a warming pad.
Apply sterile lubricant to the eyes to prevent desiccation during surgery.
Shave both groins and remove hair with moist gauze.
Prep the surgical sites with chlorhexidine/70% ethanol solution.
Drape the animal with sterile towels.
Administer Carprofen (5 mg/kg, subcutaneously) as analgesic.
Make a 4 cm long skin incision on the left groin parallel to the inguinal ligament.
Cut through the fat pad circumferentially with scissors, leaving it attached to its vascular pedicle based on the epigastric vessels.
Free the filmy connective tissue adhesions between the abdominal wall and underlying femoral vessels using micro scissors.
Place a retractor on the abdominal wall and pull medially.
Expose the inguinal ligament and the whole length of the femoral vessels.
Dissect the epigastric vein and isolate it from its surrounding fat by gently pulling and cutting.
Using micro forceps and curved micro scissors, open the perivascular sheath containing the femoral vessels from the inguinal ligament to its bifurcation distal to the epigastric branch.
Pick up the femoral vein by its adventitia with micro forceps and gently separate it from the surrounding tissues and accompanying artery.
Cut through the tissue around the vein using curved round-pointed micro scissors while pulling the tissue apart.
Ligate side branches found during dissection with 10/0 nylon suture or coagulate them with a bipolar coagulator.
Ligate the proximal and distal ends of the femoral vein with 4/0 silk sutures to obtain a vein graft of at least 10 mm length including approximately 0.5 cm length of the epigastric branch.
Trim the adventitia from the graft's ends using micro forceps and straight micro scissors by gently pulling and cutting.
Flush the vein graft with heparinized saline solution (10 U/ml of heparin).
Leave the vein graft in the heparinized saline solution to rest.
Close the wound using continuous running 4/0 silk suture plus two or three additional simple interrupted stitches.
Repeat steps 1.2.1 to 1.2.4 in the exact same way on the contralateral limb.
Dissect and isolate both the epigastric artery and vein from the surrounding fat pad using micro forceps by gently pulling the tissue away from the vessels.
Pick up the femoral artery by its adventitia with micro forceps and free it from the surrounding tissues using curved round-pointed micro scissors by pulling the tissue apart and cutting through it.
Ligate or coagulate side branches of the femoral artery.
Ligate the femoral artery and vein distal to the emergence of the epigastric vessels using 4/0 silk suture.
Place a single clamp proximally on each of the femoral artery and vein.
Make a clean transverse cut in each vessel distal to the emergence of the epigastric branches with a sharp straight micro scissor.
Flush the vessels vigorously with generous amounts of heparinized saline until all the blood is removed from the lumen.
Place a sterile plastic contrast background under the vessels.
Remove any redundant adventitia from the vessels' ends as per step 1.2.10, if needed.
Perform both microsurgical anastomoses with 10/0 nylon suture.
Anastomose the proximal end of the vein graft to the femoral vein and the distal end to the femoral artery.
Make sure the femoral vessels and the vein graft rest in their natural position without any twists.
Check for leaks at both anastomotic sites.
Resolve small leaks by placing a small piece of fat on top and gently compressing for 5-10 min.
Place additional stitches to resolve larger pulsating leaks that rapidly flood the entire field.
Check patency of the arteriovenous loop.
Gently occlude the femoral artery and vein to verify their response.
Shrink the femoral artery by gentle occlusion while making the femoral vein engorge with the same action.
Place the base of the tissue engineering chamber under the arteriovenous loop in its natural position without twists or kinks.
Secure the base of the chamber to the inguinal ligament and underlying muscle fascia with 6/0 nylon sutures.
Place the lid over the base so that the femoral vessels enter the chamber through a notch.
Close the lid, making sure it catches the epigastric branches acting as tethers to hold the arteriovenous loop into position.
Close the wound using continuous running 4/0 silk suture plus two or three additional simple interrupted stitches.
Allow the animal to recover from anesthesia on a warming pad.
Administer Carprofen (5 mg/kg, subcutaneously) as analgesic 24 hours later.
Treat the wound with topical antibiotic ointment for 5 days.
Anesthetize and close the wound if it is opened.
Monitor the health of the animal daily.

Euthanize the animal using a lethal dose of intraperitoneal lethabarb injection (163 mg/kg in 0.25 ml by 23 G needle) if more than one moderate signs of inactivity, poor appetite, weight loss, and loss of color are observed.
Repeat steps for preparation of the animal for surgery as necessary.
Isolate femoral vessels and insert the chamber following previous steps.
Place each intact femoral vessel on the corresponding slit of the chamber base ensuring no twists or kinks.
Close the chamber by attaching the lid to the base.
Close the wound using continuous running 4/0 silk suture plus two or three additional simple interrupted stitches.
Anesthetize the animal when reaching experiment's time points (4-6 weeks post-implantation).
Repeat steps for opening the wound, cutting through tissues until chamber is completely exposed.
Expose the femoral vessels proximal to the construct and test for vascular patency by gently occluding the vessel with two microforceps.
Gently milk the blood in a distal direction after occlusion.
Release the proximal forceps if the vessel fills with blood again, confirming patency.
Ligate the femoral vessels proximally in the case of the arteriovenous loop.
Ligate both proximally and distally in the case of the flow-through configuration.
Remove the chambers with containing tissue en bloc after ligature.
Euthanize the animal using a lethal dose of intraperitoneal lethobarb injection (163 mg/kg in 0.25 ml by 23 G needle).
Fix tissues in 4% paraformaldehyde at room temperature for 24 hours.
Divide tissues into multiple transverse sections (1-2 mm thick).
Embed tissues in paraffin wax or optimal cutting temperature compound for paraffin sections (5 µm) or frozen sections (10 µm), respectively.
Perform routine histological staining such as hematoxylin and eosin to examine the general morphology of tissues.
Perform immunohistochemical staining with specific antibody to identify cell type of interest, for example cardiac troponin T immunostaining for cardiomyocytes.
